result.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
result.summary: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic baseline, and where the same 3D models chained by fixed rules call progression falsely at 33 of 56 follow-ups, it does so twice. On clinical follow-up CTs, it agrees with the radiologists' response at 20 of 23 follow-ups, including every change in response, and without training on DeepLesion, it retrieves more of its lesions than every tracker trained on it (89.0% vs. 87.4%). Its harness, not its LLM, makes the difference: given the same LLM and 3D models but not the harness, Claude Code reaches a detection F1 of 41% and LesionAgent 78%, and an open-weight LLM that can run inside the hospital rises from 6% to 73%. LesionAgent and a napari reading app for any LLM are available at https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/LesionAgent.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LesionAgent：一个无需任务特定训练的 LLM agent，把冻结的 3D 模型当作工具，通过坐标标注视图在 3D 中操作，用病灶登记表跨访视记住每个病灶并核验所依赖的模型输出，数值判断交由确定性的临床指南引擎，用于纵向 CT 的病灶追踪与疗效评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「决定效果的是 harness 而非 LLM」的外置验证、记忆登记与规则计算分工，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、输出核验及数值推理是否交给确定性模块提供可核查线索；但工作属临床 3D 影像应用，与 VLM 内部 latent 表示无直接关联。
